correctness.rationale: All distances are intrinsic on explicitly defined unit-edge Cartesian graph products; a complete endpoint-route partition handles same and opposite rail copies and same/different rungs. A table of exact conditional first and second moments, with arclength weights 4m^2:4mn:n^2 for open and 4:4:1 for circular ladders, derives all formulas. The strict mean comparison reduces to a positive polynomial in n-3. Explicit couplings bound the rescaled distance error by 4/n and prove the distinct limiting distributions. The standalone rational polygon-clipping verifier independently integrates the shortest-route envelope for 14 graphs, 2401 unordered edge pairs and 4802 moment equalities, all passing. No finite check substitutes for the universal analytical proof.

evidence: Garijo et al. (2023) give an algorithm computing a fixed graph continuous mean from its endpoint graph distances, and an exact complete-graph formula; the fully accessible structural results concern complete graphs, trees, and cactus graphs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: An algorithm with general input does not by itself assert the present all-integer finite-size closed forms, second moments, strict comparison, or strong-coupling law. Its computation procedure is nevertheless acknowledged as prior art, not claimed as a new approach.

originality.rationale: The precise unit-edge open and periodic ladder first-two-arclength-moment theorem, strict finite-size comparison, and strong limit-law change were not found in actual research-index and scholarly searches. Earlier available work treats farthest-point geometry, discrete vertex Wiener polynomials, fixed-graph continuous-mean algorithms, and general mean-distance inequalities, none of which states the present symbolically uniform-in-order and squared-distance theorem. Historical-priority uncertainty from inaccessible older full text remains.

Bibliographic indexes and public research-record searches are not exhaustive; unknown or unindexed exact arclength ladder formulas remain possible.

value.rationale: This is a natural pair-distance transport quantity for growing corridor networks with two different boundary conditions. The claim supplies exact two-moment laws for every order, a nontrivial periodic parity correction, a strict comparison despite unequal normalized arclength measures, and a uniform-coupling demonstration that adding only two edges (vanishing relative length) changes the entire macroscopic law. The exact leading mean factor 3/4 and variance factor 3/8 provide useful, geometrically motivated benchmarks, not a single arbitrary numerical instance.
